questions.question: What is character encoding, and why is UTF-8 the default?
questions.answer: Encoding maps bytes to characters. UTF-8 covers all Unicode, is backward-compatible with ASCII, and is the modern required choice. Declare it with meta charset in the first bytes of head and save the file as UTF-8.

questions.question: When do you need named or numeric entities?
questions.answer: When a character collides with HTML syntax (&, <, >), is invisible (nbsp), or is hard to type. Named entities use names (©), numeric use code points (© or ©).

questions.question: Why is chaining   for layout a bad idea?
questions.answer: It creates non-breaking spaces that prevent wrapping, break responsive layout and copy-paste, and can be announced oddly by screen readers. Use CSS margins/padding for spacing.

questions.question: What does the W3C validator catch that browsers do not show?
questions.answer: Browsers silently repair many errors, so the page looks fine while the markup is invalid. The validator reports misnested tags, duplicate ids, missing alt, invalid attribute values, and disallowed children.

questions.question: What is the difference between quirks mode and standards mode?
questions.answer: The doctype selects the mode. Standards mode follows modern CSS/HTML rules; quirks mode emulates legacy behavior, changing box sizing, line heights, and table layout. Missing doctype triggers quirks mode.

questions.question: Write a paragraph that literally displays <div> and shows ₹499 with a copyright symbol.
A page shows cafÃ© instead of café. What happened and how do you fix it?
questions.answer: UTF-8 bytes were decoded as Windows-1252 or another legacy charset, producing mojibake. Add meta charset=UTF-8 early in head and re-save the file as UTF-8; do not patch with entities.

questions.question: Why can a missing doctype make a layout look different even with identical CSS?
questions.answer: Without the doctype the browser uses quirks mode, which emulates legacy box-model and layout behavior. Widths and spacing can differ from standards mode, so the same CSS renders differently.
